data.narrative:
Fuse Energy is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by JC Btaiche, currently valued at $200M+ post-money after raising $78M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a sector comp universe of 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, General Matter, and Standard Nuclear.

Stage-progression methodology applies directly to this dataset. Using the $200M last post-money valuation as a base and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression to the next institutional funding round yields an implied valuation of $400M. Peer-median analysis is not applicable; while 3 nuclear energy companies exist in the broader comp set, none meet the threshold of 3+ datapoints within the same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier necessary for reliable median extraction.

The triangulated valuation range of $340M (low) to $460M (high), with a median of $400M, rests on a single quantitative method. This methodological constraint creates material uncertainty. The range reflects reasonable bounds around stage-typical progression, but lacks the cross-validation that peer-based pricing would provide. Key uncertainties include technology de-risking velocity, regulatory pathway clarity, and the absence of sufficient narrow-peer comparables to validate market-based multiples within the nuclear energy subsector at this stage.
